chapter_theme: Being settled by listening (கேள்வி கேட்டமைதல்): hearing about the Lord, his deeds and his grace, then reciting and realising it, leads to the Siva-state and makes people like gods; but what counts is knowing him with longing, not hearing or reckoning alone.
structure_note: The chapter opens with the kinds of hearing that end in Siva-gati (300) and the order recite, listen, realise (301); it then promises godhood and grace to those who hear and speak of him (302 to 305), sets listening among the soul's supports (307), and closes on those for whom hearing is empty (306, 308, 309).

300.reading: Hearing of virtue, hearing the words of the andhanar, hearing of wrong, hearing the mantras of the gods, hearing of outer things, and hearing the ways of our gold-bodied Lord: by these the Siva-state is gained.
300.nuance: The repeated கேட்டும் can be additive (by all these hearings) or concessive (though one hears all these, it is hearing the Lord's ways that gains the goal). மறம் is taken as wrong, the opposite of அறம், or as valour; புறம் as outer or worldly matters, or other doctrines.

301.reading: Who knows the Lord of the gods, the divine form? Once you know him, recite, listen and realise; those who recited and realised stood exalted.
301.nuance: ஓதுமின் கேள்மின் உணர்மின் puts the three in order: recitation, listening, realisation, the last being the point. The first two lines can also be read 'whoever knows him'.

302.reading: If great Nandi wills, one hears Mayan's word; one hears Brahma's word through Hara's will; those who hear Siva's word become gods; to hear the word that bears fruit is the real hold.
302.nuance: பணி may be word, command or service. மயன் may be Maya the divine artificer or Vishnu (மாயன்). பற்று in the last line may be the refuge one holds to or, negatively, attachment; I read it as refuge, but the line is unclear.

303.reading: Holy people who stay saying of him 'this is the Lord' will later become gods; our First Lord, of rare tapas, gladly grants grace to the great ascetics who come to him.
303.nuance: The first half rewards speech about the Lord, the second tapas. அருமாதவத்து can describe the Lord or the tapas through which the ascetics come.

304.reading: Speaking of the Lord's grace, of death and of birth, babbling in delight, he becomes love to them and, standing as the living light, abides like the scent in a fragrant flower.
304.nuance: பிதற்றி, babbling, is praise here: the talk of the enraptured devotee. The subject shifts between the devotees and the Lord; the scent in the flower is an image of his presence, felt and unseen.

305.reading: When the mind grasps excellence, listening and the conduct of true knowledge, if it does not slip from them, one becomes, without fault, even the king of the gods for countless ages.
305.nuance: The last two lines are compressed: the one who holds fast may become the king of the gods, or the king of the gods may stay with him. வழுக்கி and இழுக்கு both carry the sense of slipping.

306.reading: Like children who belch over rice made of sand, those who think enjoyment of the Real comes by mere closeness, and who do not fix on the One that cannot be fixed, have stayed without knowing; they are not what they claim.
306.nuance: The sand-rice of children's play is food that cannot satisfy. குறியாதது, what cannot be marked or made an object, is traditionally the Supreme beyond every sign. செறிவு may be closeness, crowding or accumulation; the target of the verse is unclear beyond its mockery of pretended experience.

307.reading: Life and body are a close support; listening that reaches the world is a close support; the mind on Siva's feet is the firm support; if one seeks the support to be gained, there is no birth.
307.nuance: A graded list of supports, each repeating துணை: the bodily, the learned, and the mind fixed on Siva, which alone ends birth. The verse does not despise the first two.

308.reading: Our Lord, the Ancient One, is there for those who praise him; for those who scorn him he becomes the place of suffering; and for those who stand apart, not reciting and knowing the First with joy, he is a cow of stone.
308.nuance: A stone cow looks like a cow and gives no milk. Read with the dative, the Lord is that to those who stand apart; it is also possible to read the stone cow as the people themselves.

309.reading: Though one holds him in mind, speaks him aloud and knows him in accord, though forms do not match one another, and though the axle turns and the pin is shaken, the First comes near only to those who know him with longing.
309.nuance: The axle and linchpin (அச்சு, ஆணி) are often taken as the body as a cart failing at death; நச்சு is longing, though it can also mean poison. The lines before the last are obscure, and the verse may be saying that mind and speech alone are not enough.

links.note: Both raise listeners to the gods: the Kural's listeners, though on earth, equal the gods fed by oblation; Tirumular's hearers of Siva's word become gods.
Both picture the moral life as walking on slippery ground. The Kural gives the words of the virtuous as a staff there; Tirumular asks the mind not to slip from listening and conduct.
Both call listening a துணை, a support. The Kural makes it a staff in faltering; Tirumular places it between the body and the mind on Siva's feet in a ladder of supports.
An image without life: the Kural likens the unlearned man's good looks to a clay doll; Tirumular makes the Lord a stone cow, giving no milk, to those who neither recite nor realise him.

300 lists many hearings, of virtue, of the andhanar's words, of the gods' mantras, and ends that hearing the Lord's ways (ஈசன் திறங்கேட்டும்) gains the Siva-state (பெற்ற சிவகதி). Kural 411 ranks the wealth of the ear first among all wealth (செவிச்செல்வம் ... செல்வத்துள் எல்லாம் தலை). Tirumular keeps the Kural's ranking of listening and names the hearing that ranks first and what it yields.

301 sets an order: once you know him, recite, listen and realise (ஓதுமின் கேள்மின் உணர்மின்), and those who recited and realised stood exalted. Kural 391 has learning followed by standing in keeping with it (கற்றபின் நிற்க அதற்குத் தக). Both make learning a first step that must be completed by something else; for the Kural it is conduct, for Tirumular realisation (உணர்தல்).

301 promises that those who recite and realise (ஓதி உணர்ந்தவர்) stand exalted. 319 mocks those who say 'we can recite and know him' (ஓதி உணரவல்லோம் என்பர்) yet do not know the inner light that moves them. The same pair of verbs is praised in one verse and doubted in the other: the claim to recite and realise is not the realisation.

303 says the holy people who keep saying of him 'this is the Lord' will later become gods too (பின்னைத் தேவரும் ஆவர்). Kural 50 says the one who lives the household life as it should be lived is placed among the gods in heaven (வானுறையும் தெய்வத்துள் வைக்கப் படும்). The same promise, an earthly person counted among the gods, is attached in the Kural to right household living and in Tirumular to speaking of the Lord.

304 ends with the Lord abiding like the scent in a fragrant flower (வாச மலர்க்கந்தம் மன்னிநின்றானே) among those who speak of him in delight. 1459 has the same simile turned inward: as scent dwells in a flower, Siva's fragrance has blossomed within the soul (பூவினிற் கந்தம் ... சீவனுக்குள்ளே சிவமணம் பூத்தது). Both use the scent to name a presence that is felt and not seen; 1459 places it in the soul itself.

306 mocks those who think the experience of the Real comes by mere closeness (செறிவால் அனுபோகம்), like children belching over rice made of sand (மணற்சோற்றில் தேக்கிடுமாபோல்). Naladiyar 321 says the fool scorns the teaching of virtue as the ladle cannot taste the milk-rice it stirs (பாற்கூழை முழை சுவையுணராது). Both use food that is handled but not tasted for people near the truth who do not receive it; the pairing depends on reading செறிவு as closeness.

308 says that to those who stand apart without reciting and knowing the First, he is a cow of stone (கற்பசு), one that looks like a cow and gives no milk. 2937 says that writing the Cause on a palm leaf without the guru joining one to it is like the teat hanging on a goat's neck (ஆட்டின் கழுத்தில் அதர்). Both reach for a milkless likeness of the source of milk to describe a relation to the Lord that has the form and none of the yield.

309 says that whatever one holds in mind or speaks, the First comes near only to those who know him with longing (நச்சு உணர்ந்தார்க்கே நணுகலுமாமே). 278 faults people who call him 'our father, our Lord' but keep him within their wants and do not seek him with longing (நச்சியே அண்ணலை நாடுகிலாரே). The same word நச்சு marks in both what naming and speaking him lack.
